port.name: hollowknight
port.title: Hollow Knight
port.desc: Hollow Knight, the hand-drawn action adventure by Team Cherry, on Unity's own Android player (run natively, no emulator). You need your own copy: the GOG Linux version.
port.inst: Put the GOG Linux installer (hollow_knight_*.sh) or the installed game folder into ports/hollowknight/gamedata, then launch. The first launch builds the game on the handheld.
port.thanks: Thanks to [Team Cherry](https://www.teamcherry.com.au/) for creating Hollow Knight and its hand-drawn kingdom of Hallownest.

game.what: Hollow Knight for Linux from GOG (version 1.5.12620, Unity 6000.0.61f1): GOG's installer (hollow_knight_*.sh) or the installed game folder

questions.question: Texture quality? Medium is what this port is tested with. Fast makes the setup much shorter, with slightly less exact textures.

route.title: Unity's Android player (armv7, Mono), run natively by ua_host on the handheld's 32-bit userland

notes: StreamingAssets read as files (references to Application.streamingAssetsPath and System.IO in TeamCherry.BuildBot, TeamCherry.Cinematics (asmpatch, when built, says which reads reach System.IO)): android_data.streaming_assets = "both" puts them beside the APK (Game_Data/StreamingAssets/, 0.0 MB, also in the OBB) and asmpatch's streaming-assets patch gives those reads that folder

InControl: it picks its Android profiles at run time by the pad's name; UA_PAD_NAME names the pad as one of them knows (asmpatch --survey lists them), else the pad is an unknown controller (docs/input.md)

PlayMaker (PlayMaker.dll): asmpatch's optimizations playmaker-loopcount and playmaker-delayedevents (the same behaviour, less work every frame for every FSM: tools/asmpatch/README.md, "Optimizations")
reads the mouse and also selects UI elements: try the pad first; UA_POINTER=1 (with UA_POINTER_TOGGLE) where menus need the mouse
reads keyboard keys (Input.GetKey, 6 references): map pad buttons with UA_KEYMAP (e.g. start:escape) where the pad has no binding
Input System package (both): its desktop build has no layout for the Android player's pads: asmpatch's inputsystem-android patch registers them (docs/input.md)

text input (UI InputField, TouchScreenKeyboard, Input.inputString): Unity's soft keyboard opens ua_host's on-screen keyboard (the pad types); UA_OSK = "done" in runtime answers it at once where text does not matter (docs/input.md)

video: 0 VideoPlayers in the main data, clips {'vp8': 16}: android-data adds Hidden/VideoDecodeAndroid (keep android_data.video_shader on); VP8/VP9 and H.264 decode built in, AAC/HEVC/MP3 only with the system's libavcodec (else silent)
P/Invoke into GalaxyCSharpGlue (GalaxyCSharp), sdkencryptedappticket (com.rlabrecque.steamworks.net), steam_api (com.rlabrecque.steamworks.net): each needs an ARM library or a stub

1849 MB of BC/DXT textures (main data): the handheld GPU cannot sample them, so Unity decodes them to RGBA when loading (4-8x the memory). The textures step (convert.steps += "textures") re-encodes them as ASTC: less memory, slightly different pixels, a longer setup; off by default

BC/DXT textures decode to about 7395 MB of RGBA on the handheld (its GPU cannot sample them): more than a 1 GB device can hold next to the game. The textures step is suggested (convert.steps), re-encoding them as ASTC at the GPU's own size; remove it only for a device with the memory to spare
4999 MB: the handheld's setup needs about 2-3 times that free while it runs
